features.name: age_life_stage_bucket
features.description: Ordinal age bands: 0 for under 25, 1 for 25-34, 2 for 35-49, 3 for 50-64, 4 for 65 or older.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides ready-made life-stage thresholds, reducing the need for several raw-age splits.

features.name: education_attainment_bucket
features.description: Ordinal education_num bands: 0 for less than high school, 1 for high-school through associate range, 2 for bachelor through professional-school range, 3 for doctoral level.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates coarse attainment cut points that align with credential jumps and are easy for trees to branch on.

features.name: bachelor_level_or_higher_indicator
features.description: Binary flag for bachelor-level education or higher, using education_num 13 and above.
features.expected_model_benefit: Exposes a common credential cutoff as a single binary split.

features.name: weekly_hours_intensity_bucket
features.description: Ordinal weekly workload bands: 0 for under 35, 1 for 35-40, 2 for 41-50, 3 for 51-60, 4 for over 60.
features.expected_model_benefit: Separates part-time, standard, extended, and extreme weekly workload patterns for direct branching.

features.name: overtime_indicator
features.description: Binary flag for rows with more than 40 hours_per_week.
features.expected_model_benefit: Highlights the common 40-hour cutoff, often useful beyond raw hour magnitude.

features.name: credentialed_full_time_indicator
features.description: Binary interaction flag for bachelor-level or higher education with at least 40 weekly hours.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures a nonlinear credential-by-workload condition in one split instead of requiring two sequential splits.

features.name: capital_activity_type
features.description: Categorical capital-activity code: 0 no capital movement, 1 gain only, 2 loss only, 3 gain and loss both present.
features.expected_model_benefit: Separates no capital event, gain only, loss only, and mixed activity without relying on two separate sparse numeric fields.

features.name: net_capital_log_signed
features.description: Signed log transform of capital_gain minus capital_loss, preserving direction while compressing large magnitudes.
features.expected_model_benefit: Compresses highly skewed capital amounts while preserving direction, making threshold searches less dominated by outliers.

features.name: spouse_present_marriage_indicator
features.description: Binary flag for spouse-present marriage states in the Adult codebook, grouping marital_status codes 1 and 2.
features.expected_model_benefit: Groups spouse-present marital states into one direct split despite unordered category coding.

features.name: professional_managerial_technical_indicator
features.description: Binary flag for professional, managerial, or technical occupations in the Adult codebook, grouping occupation codes 3, 9, and 12.
features.expected_model_benefit: Combines related high-skill occupation codes so a tree can split on the group without discovering several isolated code branches.

features.name: household_responsibility_score
features.description: Integer 0-5 semantic score from marital_status, relationship, and age. Suggested anchors: 0 own-child or other-relative youth pattern, 1 non-family or unmarried adult, 2 formerly married without spouse, 3 married with spouse absent or uncertain household role, 4 spouse-present adult, 5 spouse or householder pattern age 30 and above.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds an ordered household-role summary from unordered relationship and marital categories for compact tree splits.

features.name: occupational_advancement_score
features.description: Integer 0-5 semantic score from occupation, workclass, and education_num. Suggested anchors: 0 without-pay, never-worked, or private-house-service context; 1 low-specialization service or manual roles; 2 production, transport, craft, or admin roles; 3 sales, protective, or technical roles; 4 professional specialty or self-employment; 5 executive, managerial, or professional context with college-level education.
features.expected_model_benefit: Adds an ordered employment-context summary so trees can use broad skill and stability patterns directly.
